newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian car bomb kills three near Lagos airport.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian car bomb kills three near Lagos airport.

text.p: A bomb planted in a Nigerian government car exploded and killed three occupants, officials said on Friday.

The explosion occurred on Thursday night near Murtala Muhammed International Airport, and the victims included a security official at the airport and an unidentified woman, officials at the facility said.
"It was in the vicinity of the airport that the car exploded last night," said one official by telephone from the airport in Ikeja district on the outskirts of Lagos.
"The area was immediately cordoned off by security men and an investigation is in progress," she said, adding, "We will not have much else to say until after the investigation."
Thisday newspaper reported that the airport security official killed in the incident was about to drive home when the car exploded.
It was not clear who planted the bomb, it said.
Residents of Ikeja said the explosion shook the area.
"There was a big bang around 9 p.m. (2000 GMT) (Thursday) night in Ikeja. It sounded like a mortar," said Chris Diala, a clerk in central Lagos who lives in Ikeja.
"There was power failure at the time in Ikeja and there was a lot of panic in our own compound," he said.

Nigeria, Africa's most populous nation, has been in crisis since June 1993 when the army annulled a presidential vote to restore democracy. Since January there have been a series of bomb blasts, some on military premises.
There have also been a spate of murders of high-profile individuals, the latest being the killing on Thursday in Ibadan, southwestern Nigeria, of wealthy businesswoman and politician Suliat Adedeji.
